newsitem.title: USA: Ehrlich sees modest U.S. inventory buildup - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Ehrlich sees modest U.S. inventory buildup - RFTV.

text.p: Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich on Friday said that the downward revised increase in fourth quarter Gross Domestic Product reflected weaker inventory accumulation but that this could remedied by a modest buildup in the months ahead.
"I think we might see some modest positive for inventories in the quarters ahead but it would be a very small one," Ehrlich said in a interview of Reuters Financial Television.

Asked if this would produce less than a 0.5 percent contribution to GDP to all of 1997, he said "Yes it does. I'm hesitant to number it, but the range you're indicating is probably in the right direction."
Ehrlich said also that the outlook was for price stability rather than deflation.

"I don't think we're looking at deflation, I think we're looking at stability of prices," he said, adding "we have real wage gains in the labor market but not at a rate that we can't finance through productivity."
He said that the U.S. expansion was robust enough that modest change in interest rates would not "the character of the expansion as we have it now."
